definition: A mental health clinic is a healthcare setting, often based in the community, where people with mental illness receive psychiatric and behavioural health care. In the source, it is also described as a place where services such as preventive health screening can be integrated into routine mental health treatment.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence states that people with mental illness “receive psychiatric and behavioural health care,” but the packet only explicitly describes an intervention delivered by psychiatrists and refers to a “community mental health clinic” within an “urban behavioural health system”; it does not clearly support that this is the routine scope of services (i.e., psychiatric + behavioural health care) in general terms.

The second sentence adds that preventive health screening “can be integrated into routine mental health treatment.” While the packet evaluates a preventive screening intervention at a community mental health clinic, it does not directly support the phrasing about integration into “routine mental health treatment” as a general property of mental health clinics.

The packet supports a community mental health clinic for patients with serious mental illness, but not the broader claim that it is a setting where people with mental illness in general receive psychiatric and behavioural health care.

The statement that preventive health screening can be integrated into routine mental health treatment goes beyond the source; the packet describes a preventive screening intervention in the clinic, not a general definition of the clinic as an integrated-treatment setting.
